purpose: Static cross-segment recovery of the shared transient-effect table's authored producer and reset callsites.

method.interpretation_rule: A relocation targeting 01F7:0E06 is the pooled-object factory call; the caller's AX immediate is the initializer callback offset passed to that factory.

relocated_call_sites.evidence: NE relocation source 01D7:3FC7 targets segment 3 offset 0x44FF
NE relocation source 01D7:44EA targets segment 3 offset 0x44FF

reset.known_behavior: Clears DS:87DE rows and resets DS:8806/DS:8808.

producer.label: spawn_effect_table_from_player_state
producer.condition: The player-update tail takes this branch only when object flags at +0x00 include 0x10 and object byte +0x3C is zero.
producer.callback_argument: AX=0x4519, DX=0x0000 immediately before the factory call
producer.post_call: The factory-created object is initialized by 01F7:4519, which installs 01F7:45AB and claims one DS:87DE row.

spawn.raw_word_occurrence: The little-endian word 0x4519 occurs once in segment 3, at 01F7:3909, as the immediate AX operand.

update_and_remove.pointer_occurrences: The raw segment contains 0x45AB at 01F7:4559 and 0x470C at 01F7:45BA/45E4; these are callback-pointer stores inside the table lifecycle, not additional authored producers.

direct_reference_scan.result: No direct same-program Ghidra incoming call references were emitted for these four entries.
direct_reference_scan.explanation: The authored spawn call is relocation-backed through the generic pooled-object factory with AX carrying the callback offset; update/remove are installed as object callback pointers, and reset has cross-segment NE relocations.

runtime_reachability_probe.fixture: W1L1 selected through the native cheat selector
runtime_reachability_probe.observed_player_flags: The sampled player object action word remained 0x0000 and the shared effect-table breakpoints were not reached.
runtime_reachability_probe.interpretation: The producer is statically recovered but not reached in this ordinary W1L1 idle trace; a targeted player-state trigger or controlled flag probe is still needed.

input_variant.input: KBD_right for 30 frames before each of 8 samples
input_variant.observed_action_words: 0x0000 in all eight sampled player callbacks

pre_producer_tail_probe.fixture: W1L1 main-tree native selector with KBD_right held for 30 frames before each of six samples
pre_producer_tail_probe.observed: All six tail snapshots had player action word 0x0000 and DS:656C source word 0x0000; no 44FF/4519/45AB/470C lifecycle hit followed.
pre_producer_tail_probe.interpretation: The ordinary input path does not raise the producer's 0x10 flag in this fixture; the trigger is likely a collision/death or other gameplay-state transition rather than directional input.

forced_trigger_probe.mutation: At 01F7:38EC, write player action word 0x0010 before the producer condition is evaluated.
observed: The producer branch writes object byte +0x3C from 0x00 to 0xFF.
The relocated factory 01F7:0E06 is reached with AX=0x4519.
The factory pool ledger shows occupancy 8 -> 9 and slot 1 carrying callback 0x4519 after the factory returns.
One guest frame later occupancy is back to 8; no 01F7:4519, 01F7:45AB, or 01F7:470C breakpoint is observed.
The player callback returns with action word 0x0010.
forced_trigger_probe.interpretation: The recovered condition and producer call are dynamically reachable when the 0x10 action state is supplied, and the factory visibly allocates a callback-4519 pool record. The next-frame scheduler probe now shows the record inserted at DS:7566 and 01F7:4519 entered with DS:88AE=0 and DS:880C=0; the callback clears +0x18 at its own guard, so this fixture rejects the effect before claiming a row. Static disassembly and END archive-slot correlation bound DS:88AE to a boss/end-sequence stage machine, so the remaining authored trigger is the completion/boss path rather than a normal Wind/UFO initializer.

natural_input_trigger_probe.input: KBD_leftalt held for 30 frames and latched through each player callback
natural_input_trigger_probe.observed: Samples 1-4 report scan code 0x38, DS:88BC=0x0010, player action word 0x0010, and object byte +0x3C changing from 0x00 at the producer entry to 0xFF after the callback.
natural_input_trigger_probe.interpretation: The tested authored trigger is the alternate-action keyboard bit supplied by left Alt; no debugger action-word mutation is needed to reach the producer guard. The separate forced probe remains the direct factory-allocation proof because this natural run's factory breakpoint was not independently captured.

scheduler_lifecycle_probe.fixture: W1L1 main-tree native selector with action word forced at 01F7:38EC
observed: The factory-created slot at pool offset 0x78 appears in DS:7566 with far callback 0x1997:0x4519 on the next frame.
01F7:4519 is entered with DS:88AE=0, DS:880C=0, DS:8806=0, and DS:8808=4; it clears object callback +0x18 and does not claim a row.
The following sample has no callback-4519 object, establishing immediate guard rejection rather than an unobserved list-removal race.
scheduler_lifecycle_probe.interpretation: The scheduler insertion is confirmed; the missing visible effect in the ordinary fixture is explained by the 4519 shared gate, not by an unresolved scheduler handoff.

scheduler_lifecycle_force_gate_probe.fixture: W1L1 main-tree native selector with action word forced at 01F7:38EC
scheduler_lifecycle_force_gate_probe.mutation: At the 01F7:4519 entry, write DS:88AE=1 to pass only the shared stage gate; no row or counter is directly written.
observed: 01F7:4519 increments DS:8806 from 0 to 1, installs callback 01F7:45AB at pool offset 0x78, seeds x=128, y=385, and leaves the effect row active.
The next sample enters 01F7:45AB for the same object with DS:8806=1 and updates the row to x=132, y=383 while callback 01F7:45AB remains installed.
scheduler_lifecycle_force_gate_probe.interpretation: The controlled gate pass closes the spawn -> update callback chain. It is debugger-only evidence of the state machine, not evidence that DS:88AE is set by this W1L1 player path.

remaining: Whether any non-keyboard gameplay transition also sets player object flags bit 0x10 in normal play.
Which authored completion/boss transition advances DS:88AE (or supplies DS:880C) so callback 01F7:4519 can claim a row, and which end-stage callback consumes each stage value.
Whether Wind/UFO authored declarations use the player-state producer or another producer path, and how their paths seed DS:87DE rows independently of the boss/end-stage gate.
The semantic names and level/reload triggers of the two reset callsites.
